newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil hopes longer-dated debt will reassure mkts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil hopes longer-dated debt will reassure mkts.

text.p: The National Treasury said it might issue longer-dated dollar-indexed notes (NTN-Ds) this week, which is widely viewed in the market as a bid to reassure investors that Brasilia will not tinker with forex policy.
A Treasury spokesman said policy-makers were mulling plans to issue 36-month NTN-Ds and the new paper might be offered to the market as early as Friday.
Currently, the longest maturity on a dollar-indexed Treasury note is 24 months.

The spokesman said the new notes are part of an ongoing bid to lengthen average maturities - now just 4.4 months - on the Treasury's outstanding 114.6 billion reais debt. But traders and analysts also see it as an attempt to reassure markets that the existing exchange rate policy will remain intact, at least in the medium term.
"The government wants to show investors that they won't drastically change foreign exchange policy over the next few years," said Deniz Pignatari, a chief trader on ING Barings' hedge desk in Brazil.

Dollar-indexed notes, which pay a fixed rate plus the variation in the foreign exchange rate, give investors a hedge against an acceleration in the rate of depreciation of the reais currency. Brazil's swelling trade deficit - which ended 1996 at a record $5.5 billion - has fueled speculation in the dollar futures market about a speedier depreciation, despite government assurances that no change is being contemplated.

Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said that if the Treasury decided to issue 36-month paper on Friday, it would issue about 3.0 billion reais of the longer-term paper, about half the amount of 12- and 24-month paper coming due this week.
The Treasury spokesman said he could not confirm the amount but said officials would announce the figure well before the auction.

Most Brazilian debt and currency traders anticipated good demand for the 36-month paper. They said it should offer a yield similar to a newly issued 24-month NTN-Ds, which at the last auction on December 30 yielded 11.93 percent.
The government, which downplays market rumors about a speedier depreciation of the reais, has stressed that the longer-dated paper will help improve its debt maturity profile.

"We want to slow down the pace at which we roll over debt. The end of inflation and economic stability allows the government to signal this longer-term horizon to the market," Eduardo Augusto Guimaraes told reporters Monday.
The government has made frustratingly slow progress in lengthening the maturity on its mammoth 232 billion reais domestic debt.

While maturities on weekly issues of Central Bank bonds have risen from 35 days to 56 days over the past two years, the average maturity on Treasury paper has risen to just 4.4 months from 3.8 months since January 1995.
